== Problem ==

Jami picked three equally spaced integer numbers on the number line. The sum of the first and the second numbers is 40, while the sum of the second and third numbers is 60. What is the sum of all three numbers?

<imath>\textbf{(A)}\ 70\qquad \textbf{(B)}\ 75\qquad \textbf{(C)}\ 80\qquad \textbf{(D)}\ 85\qquad \textbf{(E)}\ 90</imath>

== Solution ==

Since the integers are equally spaced, they form an arithmetic sequence, so we can label the middle term <imath>a</imath>, the smallest one <imath>a-d</imath> and the largest one <imath>a+d</imath>. We are given that <imath>(a-d)+a=2a-d=40</imath> and <imath>a+(a+d)=2a+d=60</imath>. Solving, <imath>(2a-d)+(2a+d)=4a=100</imath> so <imath>a=25</imath>. The problem asks for the sum of all 3 numbers, which is <imath>(a-d)+a+(a+d)=3a=3 \cdot 25 = \boxed{\textbf{(B)} 75}</imath>.

~mrtnvlknv

==Solution 2==

The numbers <imath> a </imath>, <imath> b </imath>, and <imath> c </imath> are equally spaced by a distance <imath> k </imath> on the number line. Then, we have <imath> b = a+k </imath> and <imath> c = a+2k </imath>. Then, the sum of the first and second numbers is <imath> a+a+k = 40 = 2a+k = 40 </imath>, and the sum of the second and third numbers is <imath> a+k+a+2k = 2a+3k = 60 </imath>. Then, solving we obtain <imath> -2k = -20 </imath>, <imath> k = 10 </imath>, and thus <imath> 2a+10 = 40 </imath>, <imath> a= 15 </imath>. Then, <imath> b=25 </imath>, and <imath> c=35 </imath>. The sum of all three is <imath> 15+25+35 = 70+5 = \boxed{\textbf{(B)} 75} </imath>.

~Pinotation

==Solution 3==

The difference of the sum of the first two integers and the sum of the last two integers differs by <imath>20</imath>. Hence, the common difference of the arithmetic sequence must be <imath>10</imath>. The only way for the sum of two integers in an arithmetic sequence with common difference 10 to have a sum ending in <imath>0</imath> is for all the integers to end in either <imath>0</imath> or <imath>5.</imath>

Testing <imath>5</imath> and <imath>15</imath> and <imath>10</imath> and <imath>20</imath> does not meet the required sum for the first two integers in the sequence. However, the sum of <imath>15</imath> and <imath>25</imath> is equivalent to <imath>40,</imath> and adding <imath>35 (25+10)</imath> to <imath>25</imath> matches up with the sum of the last two integers, <imath>60.</imath> Consequently, the arithmetic sequence is <imath>15, 25, 35,</imath> with a common difference of <imath>10.</imath> Adding up all the terms in the sequence gives the answer, <imath>15+25+35=\boxed{\textbf{(B)} 75}</imath>

~zoyashaikh

==Solution 4, (the most complicated, just math)==

<cmath>x + y = 40</cmath> (equation 1)
<cmath>y + z = 60</cmath> (equation 2)
<cmath> x = a, y = a + d, z = a + 2d</cmath> 
<cmath>x + x + d = 40</cmath> (equation 1)
<cmath>x + d + x + 2d = 40</cmath> (equation 2)
<cmath>(2x + 3d) - (2x + d) = 20</cmath> (eqs. 1 and 2 subtracted)
<cmath>2d = 20, d = 10</cmath>
<cmath>2a + 10 = 40, a = 15</cmath> (substitute)
<cmath>a + a + d + a + 2d = 15 + 15 + 10 + 15 + 20 = \boxed{75}</cmath> (plug in and substitute)
